questions.q: What does the JML model stand for, and what does it describe?
options: Join, Merge, Lock — a database replication pattern
Joiners, Movers, Leavers — the three identity lifecycle events that require an access change
Job, Manager, Location — three fields stored in an HR record
Just-in-time Minimal Logins — a method for granting temporary access only
questions.explain: JML names the three moments in a person's relationship with an organization where their access needs to change: joining, moving, and leaving.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real risk with access granted at onboarding (the joiner event)?
options: New hires are always given too little access to do their job
It becomes the permanent floor and is rarely re-examined after the first day
Onboarding access automatically expires after 90 days in every organization
There is no risk — joiner access is the safest part of the identity lifecycle
questions.explain: Whatever access is granted on day one tends to stick around indefinitely, because nothing in most processes forces a second look.

questions.q: Why are mover events described as the quietest source of access risk?
options: Role changes always result in a complete loss of all prior access
Movers are not tracked by any identity system at all
Mover events only happen once per employee's entire career
New access gets granted quickly because it unblocks work, but old access is often not removed because removing it creates no urgency
questions.explain: Granting access is urgent because it blocks productivity; removing old access isn't, so it's frequently skipped — this is how access creep accumulates.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, why did Maria's SQL Server login and file-server group membership survive her termination?
options: The HR system intentionally delays all de-provisioning by 18 months
SQL Server logins can never be disabled once created
Neither was tied to her Active Directory account, so the HR-driven termination process had no way to find and revoke them
Her manager explicitly approved keeping her access active after she left
questions.explain: Access granted outside the main HR-to-IT pipeline — like a manually created login or a legacy group — isn't visible to the systems that fire on a leaver event.

options: The formal process of granting a new hire their first access bundle
A type of malware that spreads through unused user accounts
A required step in every leaver de-provisioning checklist
The gradual, undocumented accumulation of access rights a user no longer needs, typically from unremoved access after role changes
questions.explain: Access creep is the buildup of unnecessary access over time, most commonly from mover events where old access isn't cleaned up.
